scope: Two independently armed windows on the actual Xboard application: native administrator HTTP device_limit apply and exact original-value restore for the sole owned synthetic ordinary user. No explicit NodeSyncService push was invoked by this helper. Each window observed the normal HTTP administrator save/Observer/node_sync queue/Redis/WSS property-update path and four working proxy bindings. UUIDs were unchanged.
administrator_authentication: Existing administrator, using only the separately owned ephemeral Sanctum bearer; administrative route and bearer remain private
original_value_source: Root-private snapshot of the actual synthetic user row; no assumed default
observer: Native UserObserver registration was independently confirmed. The HTTP helper only submitted the device_limit field and did not invoke the observer, queue job or push service directly.
observation: Each apply/restore window used its own private journal cursor and PID/credential checks. Unique traditional users-delta messages and machine users-updated messages were mapped to the four owned bindings; connected WebSockets skipped REST polling. Proxy probes then used the unchanged current UUID.
privacy: No UUIDs, token values, password hashes, administrative URI, private user snapshot, journal cursors or secret fingerprints are published. Detailed evidence remains in Root-private lab directories.
limits: This is a normal administrator HTTP property-update test with an unchanged UUID; it does not establish hitless UUID rotation.
It does not overwrite run004: the CLI UUID-save-only test did not observe expected Observer messages and its cause remains unresolved.
It does not overwrite the actual upstream Xray UUID-update failures in run003 full-sync and run005 single-user delta; those remain failures and limitations.
It verifies property-update delivery and continuing proxy authentication; it does not prove device-limit enforcement at the configured threshold.
Final Node/Root/plugin cleanup and final rebuilt-package validation are separate phases.
